iWant: Squire to set up my Cloudflare account once so nothing there can cost me money, and to put sites live only when I say yes
soThat: a website never costs me money or goes live by surprise
description: The website journey: the one-off safe set-up, the deploy-only token, a preview, and live on a yes. Live on a yes is the safety story's criterion that nothing is sent or goes live without the Squire owner's yes, met again here for websites.
title: Websites: a safe Cloudflare set-up, preview first, live on yes

acceptanceCriteria.description: After the one-off Cloudflare set-up, everything that could cost the Squire owner money there is switched off and a spend guard is on.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A Cloudflare account set up through Squire's one-off set-up
acceptanceCriteria.when: The account's settings are read after set-up
acceptanceCriteria.then: Every paid feature is off, the spend guard is on, and the short-lived set-up token has been removed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Squire deploys a site with a deploy-only token and shows the Squire owner a preview first.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A Cloudflare account set up through Squire's one-off set-up, and a site Squire has built for the Squire owner
acceptanceCriteria.then: The token Squire deploys with can deploy and nothing else, and the Squire owner has been shown the site as a preview first.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A feature or subscription on the Cloudflare account that Squire's one-off set-up cannot read as free counts as paid, and the set-up does not report done.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A Cloudflare account going through Squire's one-off set-up, on which the set-up finds a feature or subscription it cannot read as free
acceptanceCriteria.when: The set-up reads the account's features and subscriptions
acceptanceCriteria.then: That feature or subscription counts as paid: the set-up names it to the Squire owner and does not report done.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When Squire's deploy has put a site live, Squire reports it live at its address once the address serves the site's page to an ordinary client, and never tells the Squire owner that a live site is not live.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A site Squire has deployed on the Squire owner's yes, through the set-up's account
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire reads the site's address back after the deploy
acceptanceCriteria.then: Once the address serves the site's page to an ordinary client, Squire reports the site live at its address. When the address refuses Squire's own read for a reason that is not "not live yet", Squire says it could not confirm the site and names the address for the Squire owner to open. Squire never tells the Squire owner that a live site is not live, and never advises a new deploy for a site that is live.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When Cloudflare does not accept the set-up token on the account's path but accepts it on the user path, Squire's one-off set-up tells the Squire owner that the set-up token must be an account-owned token and where to make it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A set-up token the Squire owner made under their own profile, not the account
acceptanceCriteria.then: The set-up tells the Squire owner that the set-up token must be an account-owned token and where to make it: Manage account, then Account API Tokens. It makes nothing on the account and keeps nothing, as for any set-up token Cloudflare does not accept.
